writeup.headline: Ensign Group rates Hold: solid growth and raised guidance, offset by weak price trend and missing cash-flow data.
writeup.thesis: Ensign Group scores 56, a Hold, with no single factor pulling it strongly either way. Growth is decent at 59, with TTM revenue growth of 17.5% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 14.5% year on year, though growth slowed by 2.8 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 52 on a 9.0% operating margin and a 20.8% gross margin, with modest dilution (diluted share count up 0.6% year on year). Valuation scores 57: in absolute terms a P/S of 1.9x is moderate and an EV/EBIT of 20.7x is not low, and both multiples sit near the middle of their own history. News is the strongest factor at 68 after the company raised 2026 EPS guidance to $7.94–$8.02, while the trend score of 45 reflects shares 10.2 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and price 14.7% below its 52-week high.
key_risks: A pending securities class action tied to the June short-seller reports, plus a reported but unverified DOJ civil investigative demand.
Heavy reliance on Medicare and Medicaid revenue leaves results exposed to reimbursement changes.
Revenue growth is slowing: growth slowed by 2.8 pp from the previous quarter.
New Florida and Texas deals will take a year or more to contribute, adding integration risk.
Weak relative price performance, with shares down 5.8% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago.
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 9 more points, for example a stronger trend score if the shares recover toward their 52-week high and close the gap with SPY.
Renewed growth acceleration or margin expansion lifting the growth and quality scores would push the score up.
A drop of 12 points to below 45 would mean Sell, for instance if the litigation or DOJ matter turns materially negative and drags the news score down.
Further growth slowdown or a rerating of the multiples above their historical middle would weigh on growth and valuation.
